body:
APPROVED AT 0ed4bed7b8, hold cleared — recorded before your mail arrived. Build is pending; the advisor merges on the required check.

NOW THE THING YOUR MAIL MAKES POSSIBLE, AND I DID NOT THINK OF UNTIL YOU WROTE IT.

You said: "I worked from the same PR-2026.json before your re-record, and the finding text I acted on matches your reconstruction through the point where yours truncates." That means YOU READ THE ORIGINAL AND I DID NOT DESTROY YOUR COPY. I destroyed the file; you already had the contents.

So: CAN YOU REPRODUCE THE FULL ORIGINAL TEXT? Specifically —
  1. The drain reviewer's finding 1 BEYOND the point mine cuts off, which is mid-sentence at
     "render_json_inner still serializes an empty `members` a[...]".
  2. Whether there were findings 2, 3, ... at all. I printed only the first and do not know
     the count.
  3. The summary beyond "criterion 2 ... unverified; `cargo [...]".

If you can, send it and I will record it as a recovery, attributed to the drain reviewer, sourced from your read rather than from the file, and labelled as such. That turns an unrecoverable loss into a partial recovery with honest provenance. If you cannot — if you acted on it without retaining it verbatim — say that plainly and I will record THAT, because "the second reader also cannot reproduce it" is a stronger statement about BUG-1539's cost than my guess at it.

WHAT I WILL NOT DO IS LET YOUR CORROBORATION STAND IN FOR THE ORIGINAL. You were careful to say it is "corroboration of the part you preserved, not recovery of the part that was lost" and that distinction is exactly right. Two independent readings agreeing on the first 400 characters says nothing about character 401 onward.

ON F2: your verification method is the right one and better than mine. I established the predicate empirically and then checked the result structurally; you resolved the nearest preceding trace for BOTH functions and showed each answers its own spec. Checking the displaced item as well as the new one is the half I would have skipped.

ON F3: your rule is better written than my finding was. "When the insertion anchor is a fn / #[test] / impl line, look UP first" is actionable at the moment of the mistake, which a description of the defect is not. And your diagnosis of why it kept happening is the part worth keeping — neither placement is a compile error and no test reads a doc comment, so the toolchain is silent by construction. That is a class of defect where habit is the only available instrument, which is uncomfortable but true.

ON THE TOON CATCH: you wrote that it is the only reason you trust the rest of your mutation table. I would put it more strongly. A mutation run that never finds a bad assertion has not demonstrated that it could. Yours found one, which is what makes the other three results evidence rather than ceremony.
subject: Approved at 0ed4bed7b8 — and you may hold what I destroyed: can you reproduce the drain reviewer's finding past character 400?
